title: Link-throttle birthmarking probe: intermittent NVLink/NCCL throughput drops and clock-domain correlation
body:
Summary:

We observed sporadic 15–45% dropouts in inter-GPU aggregate bandwidth during pipeline+tensor parallel runs on a 4x-H100 node cluster. The drops are short-lived (20–200ms) but correlate with increased token latency tails and NCCL retries on collective ops. This doc records a reproducible birthmarking test and early root-cause hypotheses (clock-domain transitions and link-level throttling), measurement techniques, quick mitigations we validated, and next tests to isolate HW vs SW.
body_2:
Context and why this matters:

- Production inference workloads with interleaved micro-batches are sensitive to short hits in cross-GPU bandwidth. Even sub-200ms bandwidth dips cause KV-cache refill stalls and token tail spikes.
- Existing NCCL perf baselines looked fine in steady-state; the transient nature means standard large-scale throughput tests miss it.
- We need a lightweight birthmarking harness that intentionally stresses link-level behavior while being easy to run in CI and on Dedicated clusters.
body_3:
Hardware and software baseline:

- Node: 4x NVIDIA H100 SXM, DGX-like backplane (NVLink fabric + PCIe host).
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15 with our production kernel tweaks.
- Driver/CUDA/NCCL: NVIDIA driver 545.xx, CUDA 12.1, NCCL 2.17.
- Serving runtime: runtime v0.42.1 (collector hooks enabled).
- Observed on mixed rack-level placements and also when all GPUs are local to the same host.

Commands to gather baseline topology and clocks:
- nvidia-smi topo -m
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,index,clocks.gr,clocks.sm,clocks.mem,pstate --format=csv
- nvlinkstat (internal shim) to sample per-link throughput (traces to /tmp/nvlink.log)
- perf counters via nvidia-smi dmon and nvprof for early correlation

Note: we captured synchronized timestamps (host-clock NTP + GPU monotonic) to align traces across nodes where applicable.
body_4:
Birthmarking harness (how to reproduce):

- Purpose: create deterministic short-window heavy allreduce/alltoall traffic with intermittent host/CPU activity to try and trigger link gating.
- Steps (shell pseudocode):
  1) build small NCCL microbench (modified simpleAllReduce) with configurable message sizes and random inter-burst jitter.
  2) run under controlled P2P placement: ranks pinned to GPUs 0..3, CPU cores isolated.
  3) concurrently run a lightweight host driver poll loop that intentionally toggles low-power features (simulate powermgr events): a loop that runs cpufreq-set between two governors at 100ms intervals.
  4) collect nvlinkstat and nvidia-smi dmon logs.

- Example run: ./nccl_microbench --algo=allreduce --msg=256KB --iters=5000 --burst-interval=50ms --jitter=10ms > run.log 2>&1 &
- Start nvlinkstat recorder: ./nvlinkstat --sample-ms=10 --out=/tmp/nvlink.log

We observed consistent dips when the host poll loop toggled power/clock hints. Remarkably, similar dips occurred without the host toggler but with synthetic host DMA bursts (fio staged reads) that coincide with PCIe activity; suggests a host-to-fabric interaction is possible.
body_5:
What we measured (high-level):

- nvlinkstat timeseries shows per-link bandwidth drop from ~180 GB/s aggregate down to 110–140 GB/s in windows of 30–180ms.
- NCCL logs show retries and increased kernel launch latency co-occurring with the link dip windows.
- GPU clocks (sm, mem) sometimes transiently drop 10–20% during the event.
- Host PCIe counters show bursts of DMA read/write at start of events.
- No consistent thermal spikes were observed (junction temps steady).

Representative excerpt (timeline):
- t0: steady state allreduce throughput.
- t0+1.2s: host DMA bursts appear (fio).
- t0+1.25s -> t0+1.4s: nvlink aggregate drops ~35%. NCCL reports 2x retry on ring transfer.
- t0+1.45s: throughput recovers; GPU clocks restore.

This pattern was reproducible across two different chassis and GPU batches, reducing likelihood of single-card defect.
body_6:
Hypotheses (ranked):

1) Link gating due to clock-domain transitions: host activity triggers a transient reassignment or gating of NVLink lanes to/from PCIe (fabric arbitration), reducing effective link width briefly.
2) Driver power-management interactions: driver or NVLink firmware enters a low-power microstate when it detects host interrupts; the transition/resume has non-trivial latency.
3) NCCL scheduling + kernel launch contention: bursts of host activity saturate the host staging path causing queuing/serialization that appears as link slowdown at GPU side.
4) Microcode/fabric bug: less likely but plausible given specific driver/firmware combo.
body_7:
Quick mitigations tested (results):

- Pinning GPUs to keep PCIe DMA paths stable: small improvement (~5–8% fewer events).
- Disabling CPU governor toggling in the experiment (simulate customer config): event rate drops markedly.
- Forcing persistent kernels / keepalive traffic (small periodic NVLink traffic) helped reduce event magnitude — suggests cold-start of some link microstate contributes.
- NCCL env tweaks (NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL) temporarily reduced retries but didn't eliminate dips.

Actionable short-term: document recommended host config for Dedicated fleet: set cpufreq governor to performance, disable aggressive PCI ASPM, set driver parameters to prefer persistent NVLink. We'll add these to the node bootstrap profile and validate across 10 nodes.
body_8:
Deeper isolation experiments (next steps):

1) Firmware/driver matrix: test across 3 driver versions and 2 firmware revs to look for regression boundaries.
2) Fabric-only probe: run identical workload with GPU->GPU transfers bypassing host staging (if possible) to see if host DMA is causal.
3) Per-link microbench: use a microbench that exercises single NVLink pairs while monitoring lane-level error counters.
4) Trace NCCL internals: enable NCCL debug trace to see exact coll op boundary timings.
5) Kernel-level capture: use NVIDIA's nvtx ranges + our perf collector to map kernel launch->complete times to link dips.
6) Try H-to-H (host-to-host) heavy DMA to see if identical dips happen without GPUs (indicates PCIe link arbitration issue).

I'll schedule the above across the staging cluster over the next 2 weeks and capture a matrix of runs.
body_9:
Hypothesis tests we consider decisive:

- If fabric-only probe (peer-to-peer, no host staging) still triggers dips: hardware fabric arbitration or NVLink microstate bug likely.
- If older driver avoids dips: driver regression -> coordinate with NVIDIA.
- If forcing persistent tiny NVLink traffic eliminates dips: cold-link resumption latency is root cause and we can mitigate by runtime-level keepalives or NCCL tweaks.
body_10:
Logging & observability improvements to add to runtime:

- Add lightweight nvlinkstat integration into our runtime trace pipeline (sample every 50ms) for production nodes behind dedicated pools.
- Emit NCCL op-level events to our tracing backend so we can fuse NCCL retry windows with link-level traces.
- Add an anomaly detector alert for short-duration >20% drop in aggregate link throughput correlated with >10ms increase in token tail latency.

This will help accelerate detection in customer clusters and avoid chasing noisy signals in ad-hoc experiments.
body_11:
Notes to self / informal observations:

- This problem is subtle: steady-state probes look fine. Need short-sample high-resolution traces.
- Customer call last month reported similar tail spikes; might be the same root cause.
- Consider adding microbench to our CI (nightly on a small lab node) to catch regressions if driver/firmware causes reappearance.

Logged by: Maya (primary), Ethan (trace analysis), Leah (kernel-level debugging).

Next-sync: 2025-03-03 10:00 PST (quick run status + firmware test scheduling).
notes: References to other docs: see /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/pcie-nvlink-host-staging-tail-latency-notes.json (related) but this probe focuses on brief link gating and birthmarking methodology, not steady-state saturation experiments.
